clue.text: Measure of keenness to offer unflattering comments about big name

indicators.note: the word for slanderous talk goes round the celebrity, as 'about' means surrounding

parts.note: to throw or sling mud is to make damaging remarks, so mud is unflattering comment
a big name is a star, a celebrity

explanation.surface: A critic sizing up how eager someone is to rubbish a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'keen as mustard' makes mustard the yardstick of eagerness.

clue.text: Musical instrument degrees — about the limit?

indicators.note: the two degrees go round the edge, as 'about' means surrounding

parts.note: MA and BA are two university degrees
a rim is an outer limit or edge

explanation.surface: Is a musical instrument worth degrees, or is that pushing it?
explanation.definitionFit: The marimba is a wooden percussion instrument struck with mallets.

clue.text: Rather moist sauce included amongst goods? On the contrary

indicators.note: the sauce seems to be placed inside, among the goods, in the surface reading
this reverses the previous instruction, so the goods go inside the sauce instead

parts.note: soy is a sauce
G is the abbreviation for good, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A damp sauce spilt among merchandise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' overturns 'included amongst', so the insertion runs the opposite way to the surface reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Soggy means wet through, more than just a little damp.

clue.text: Hibernating snake securing shelter

indicators.note: the snake holds on to the shelter by enclosing it

parts.note: an asp is a snake
lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: A snake hibernating safely in its refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: A hibernating creature is in a deep winter sleep.

clue.text: Lay out odd parts of diet: odd bits of cake

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters, first and third, of the word diet are taken
again the odd-numbered letters, first and third, of the word cake are taken

explanation.surface: Planning a diet with occasional crumbs of cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd parts of' and 'odd bits of' each signal the same selection, odd-numbered letters; 'Lay out' means floor someone, not arrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck someone is to knock them flat with a punch.

clue.text: Sailor's first of us tucking into fruit and rare food

indicators.note: the sailor and letter are tucked inside the fruit, as 'tucking into' means going inside

parts.note: a plum is a fruit
AB, able-bodied seaman, is the crossword sailor

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word 'us' is taken

explanation.surface: A sailor tucking into fruit, alongside some unusual dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rare food' means a rare word for food, not food that is scarce.
explanation.definitionFit: Pabulum is an uncommon, rather literary word for nourishment or sustenance.

clue.text: Right-winger supporting professional male working in coastal area

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, at the end

parts.note: pro is short for professional
on means working, as a switched-on machine
a Tory is a British Conservative

explanation.surface: A Conservative backing a professional man at work on the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A promontory is a headland jutting into the sea.

clue.text: Vegetable convention, perhaps, held around Southern French city

indicators.note: the vegetable is held round the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a bean is a vegetable
con is short for a convention, as in a comic con

explanation.surface: A vegetable-growers' gathering hosted in a southern French town.
explanation.definitionFit: Besançon is a city in eastern France near the Swiss border.

clue.text: Beautiful appearance given to instrument quickly!

parts.note: good looks are a beautiful appearance
a harp is a musical instrument

explanation.surface: A musical instrument given a handsome finish.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Look sharp!' is an idiom urging someone to hurry up.

clue.text: Reticence of the writer penning poetry ending in neglect

indicators.note: the writer's word holds the poems, as a pen encloses

parts.note: my is the writer's possessive, of the writer
odes are poems

indicators.note: the final letter of 'neglect' is used

explanation.surface: A poet whose reserve shows in neglected verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Modesty is a reserved, self-effacing manner, as reticence is.

clue.text: Genuine about Government, like many a ruler

indicators.note: the word for genuine goes round the abbreviation, as 'about' means surrounding

parts.note: genuine means real

explanation.surface: A real government, of the sort many monarchs lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Regal means kingly or royal, the manner of many monarchs.

clue.text: Interrupt discussion, and here we are?

parts.note: to cross someone is to get in their way or thwart them, a kind of interrupting
a word, as in 'can I have a word?', is a brief discussion

explanation.surface: Someone butting into a conversation, then a knowing wink at the reader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here we are?' points at the very puzzle being solved.
explanation.definitionFit: The solver is, at this moment, inside a crossword puzzle, so the self-reference identifies it.

clue.text: Just over four weeks border uproar

parts.note: May has 31 days, slightly more than four weeks
a hem is the border of a garment

explanation.surface: A month of trouble along a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayhem is chaos and disorder, much the same as uproar.

clue.text: Beach alarm blocked by old unspecified people

indicators.note: the abbreviation for old blocks the run of letters by sitting inside it

parts.note: sand makes up a beach
SOS is the distress signal

explanation.surface: A beach warning obstructed by some elderly folk.
explanation.definitionFit: So-and-sos are people one cannot or will not name, often used disparagingly.

clue.text: Gag spinner reeling off spicy, crunchy stuff

indicators.note: reeling is staggering about, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A comedian rattling off jokes while munching spicy snacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Gingersnaps are crisp biscuits flavoured with ginger.

clue.text: Historic Queen, one from Scotland with a second name

indicators.note: the extra letter is added as a second copy beside the one already there

parts.note: ane is the Scots word for one

explanation.surface: A queen of old, a Scot with a middle name.
explanation.walkthrough: ANE already has one N; 'with a second' adds another.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne was a historical English and British queen, the last Stuart monarch.

clue.text: Queen meeting scoundrel in uncomplicated story

indicators.note: the queen and scoundrel go inside the word for uncomplicated

parts.note: naive means simple, unsophisticated
R, for regina, means queen
a rat is a scoundrel

explanation.surface: A queen meeting a villain in a simple tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative is an account of events, a story.

clue.text: Reference work: it's recalled in study probing personal record

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: a diary is a personal record

indicators.note: the reversed pair goes inside the word for study

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study

indicators.note: the little word is called back, so read in the reverse direction

parts.note: the word it, with the 's meaning 'is' as a link

explanation.surface: A reference book being remembered while studying somebody's diary.
explanation.walkthrough: In 'it's' the 's is just 'is', a link; 'recalled', 'in' and 'probing' then nest three pieces one inside another. Con, to study, is an archaic verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A dictionary is the archetypal reference book.

clue.text: Positive mistake inducing rage in man with a keen sense

indicators.note: the mistake takes in the rage, leading it inside

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake
to fume is to rage

explanation.surface: A clear error that enrages a sharp-nosed man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keen sense' is smell; a perfumer blends scents.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfumer needs an acute sense of smell to create scents.

clue.text: Aspiring woman to move quickly, reversing large lorry

parts.note: to career is to rush headlong

indicators.note: a lorry reversing goes backwards, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: a rig is an articulated lorry, chiefly in American usage

explanation.surface: An ambitious woman dashing about while backing up a big truck.
explanation.definitionFit: A career girl is a woman ambitious to succeed in her profession.

clue.text: Dull person getting a couple of books in prison

indicators.note: the article and books are placed inside the prison

parts.note: a cage confines like a prison
B is the abbreviation for book, so two are BB

explanation.surface: A boring inmate given a couple of books in jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabbage is slang for a dull, inactive person.

clue.text: Small drug advertisement

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A little advert for some narcotic.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot is a short slot for a commercial on TV or radio.

clue.text: Muscle having instant power? Singular

parts.note: a trice is an instant

explanation.surface: Is there a uniquely instant way to power up a muscle?
explanation.definitionFit: The triceps is the large muscle at the back of the upper arm.

clue.text: Access point or spot ultimately gaining entry to China

indicators.note: the letters enter the friend's name, going inside

parts.note: china means friend (rhyming slang china plate, mate), so pal

indicators.note: the last letter of 'spot' is taken

explanation.surface: A doorway or site eventually letting someone into China.
explanation.definitionFit: A portal is a gateway or doorway, a way in.

clue.text: Yorkshire city supporter with no change in degree?

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
D, short for degree, swapped for D, or D FOR D, leaves the degree unchanged

explanation.surface: A fan from a northern city whose qualification never altered.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'D for D' literally: replacing D with D changes nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Bradford is a large city in West Yorkshire in northern England.

clue.text: Pretentious person rejected excellent small plant

indicators.note: the word is thrown back, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: a snob is pretentious
A1 means first-rate, written here as AI

explanation.surface: A snob spurned a fine miniature plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonsai is a tree kept tiny by careful pruning in a pot.

clue.text: Agreed to accept $1000 increase

indicators.note: the agreeing word takes the letter in

parts.note: 'sure' expresses agreement
a grand, G, is a thousand dollars

explanation.surface: A deal agreed to take a thousand-dollar rise.
explanation.definitionFit: A surge is a sudden rise, an increase.

clue.text: No end of writing experts

indicators.note: the final letter of the word for writing is dropped

parts.note: prose is ordinary writing

explanation.surface: Experts writing endlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Pros are professionals, skilled experts.

clue.text: Romania is misplaced in this part of the world

indicators.note: letters put in the wrong places are rearranged

explanation.surface: A geography slip, putting Romania in the wrong region.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia Minor is the historic name for the Anatolian peninsula, a region of the world.

clue.text: Soldiers, on reflection, will be found among the fit

indicators.note: the reversed letters sit amid the letters of 'the'
a reflection shows a mirror image, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers thinking it over among the able-bodied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' is a noun here, a spasm, not 'healthy'.
explanation.definitionFit: A throe is a violent spasm or pang, as a fit is.

clue.text: Facial application: variety of dye injected into skin opening — revolutionary

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are put inside the reversed word
revolving turns things round, so read backwards

parts.note: a pore is a tiny opening in the skin

indicators.note: a variety of the word is a different arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A cosmetic procedure injecting a radical dye into the skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns the skin opening round to EROP, and 'variety of' jumbles the colour word before it is injected.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye-drops are applied to the eyes, part of the face.

clue.text: Very good fans, nothing less — fans of 10?

parts.note: 'very good' and 'so' are both expressions of assent

indicators.note: the letter for nothing is subtracted from the word

parts.note: lovers of something are its fans
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Keen enthusiasts, no fewer, devoted to the puzzle at 10.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is CROSSWORD; its fans are those who solve it.
explanation.definitionFit: Solvers are the people who enjoy tackling crosswords.
